correctness.rationale: For the full-logarithm Hilbert cross-ratio metric on arbitrary Euclidean simplices, the Dirichlet exponential representation gives the exact identity \(D_{ab}=\log\max_i(E_{ai}/E_{bi})+\log\max_i(E_{bi}/E_{ai})\). Each single-coordinate threshold violation with denominator label \(b\) has probability \(\mathbb E\max_a(E_a/x_{ab})/N+O(N^{-2})\), while simultaneous violations for different denominators have probability \(O(N^{-2})\), by the proved largest-exponential argument. Across independent coordinate columns this yields the independent denominator-block factorization and complete joint limit. The single-ratio exact CDF supplies uniform exponential tails of centered log maxima and thus convergence of all fixed joint moments. The Hoeffding covariance integral evaluates exactly to \(\pi^2/9\) through a Frullani integral and a Fourier-dilogarithm identity. Distinct incident edges share exactly one dependent block; disjoint edges are independent. Numerical assertions passed, but universal correctness rests on the analytical proof.

value.rationale: Pairwise projective distances among uniform random points in an increasing-dimensional simplex form a natural complete finite metric signature. One-point marginal limit alone cannot predict dependence between triangle sides; the theorem determines the full finite-point joint law, proves disjoint independence, and shows a nonzero, exact and sample-count-independent one-third correlation precisely for incident edges. This is a structural geometric-probability classification with a recognizable edge-incidence covariance law, not a numeric special case, not a routine normalization test, and not an arbitrarily selected subparameter.
